/**
 * One immutable SoA row directory over two reference planes and unsigned state bytes.
 * Each row is an occurrence: repeated physical indexes retain repeated values. Captured
 * arrays are privately copied once; slicing shares them, stable sorting permutes only
 * primitive indexes, and masking builds an indexed selection. No Map.Entry is retained.
 *
 * <p>Typed adapters materialize independent M3-backed JDK, Guava, Eclipse Collections,
 * Spring and Apache Commons Collections results. These are distinct provider contracts:
 * list-valued multimaps count occurrences; Spring size() counts keys; sorted sets remove
 * comparator-equivalent duplicates; JDK Map overwrites repeated keys. The provider's
 * public interface, views and mutation rules remain owned by its actual library.
 * The results are <em>detached</em>, unlike the separate live M3FilteredViews wrappers.
 *
 * <p>JNI is opt-in and reuses the existing {@link M3IndexMaskWindow} C17 primitive
 * selector. Java predicates, comparators, keys, values and object pointers never enter
 * JNI. NATIVE_REQUIRED never silently falls back. Not thread-safe during construction,
 * not a serializable concrete vendor class, and no throughput superiority is presumed.
 */
public final class M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> {
    private final Object[] keys;
    private final Object[] values;
    private final byte[] states;
    private final int[] rows;
    private final int from;
    private final int to;

    private M3FiveLibraryIndexViews(Object[] keys, Object[] values, byte[] states,
            int[] rows, int from, int to) {
        this.keys = keys;
        this.values = values;
        this.states = states;
        this.rows = rows;
        this.from = from;
        this.to = to;
    }

    /**
     * Capture aligned payload/state planes, plus an occurrence-order index lane.
     * Indexes must be physical positions, not signed payload IDs or tombstones;
     * zero and repeated indexes are valid. No input array is retained.
     */
    public static <K, V> M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> capture(
            K[] keys, V[] values, int[] orderedRows, byte[] physicalStates) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(keys, "keys");
        Objects.requireNonNull(values, "values");
        Objects.requireNonNull(orderedRows, "orderedRows");
        Objects.requireNonNull(physicalStates, "physicalStates");
        if (keys.length != values.length || keys.length != physicalStates.length) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("payload and state planes differ in length");
        }
        for (int row : orderedRows) Objects.checkIndex(row, keys.length);
        Object[] keyCopy = keys.clone();
        Object[] valueCopy = values.clone();
        byte[] stateCopy = physicalStates.clone();
        int[] rowCopy = orderedRows.clone();
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keyCopy, valueCopy, stateCopy,
                rowCopy, 0, rowCopy.length);
    }


    /**
     * LeetCode #1920-style ordinal gather into a detached int[] index lane.
     * Repeated ordinals intentionally retain repeated logical occurrences;
     * payload keys/values/states remain in the same privately captured arrays.
     */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> takeOrdinals(int[] ordinals) {
        int[] selected = M3ArrayifiedIndexOps.gather(rows, from, to, ordinals);
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, selected, 0, selected.length);
    }

    /** LeetCode #189: triple-reversal rotation on an index window only. */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> rotated(int distance) {
        int[] selected = M3ArrayifiedIndexOps.rotated(rows, from, to, distance);
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, selected, 0, selected.length);
    }

    /**
     * LeetCode #27 two-pointer selection over per-logical-occurrence mask bytes.
     * Unlike the existing physical-state filter, repeated physical rows may
     * have different occurrence-level states. Explicit JNI reuses the existing
     * mask position selector; no objects or Java callbacks cross JNI.
     */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> selectedByOccurrenceStates(
            byte[] occurrenceStates, int required, int excluded,
            M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend backend) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(occurrenceStates, "occurrenceStates");
        if (occurrenceStates.length != size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("state mask must align with logical occurrences");
        }
        int[] selected = M3ArrayifiedIndexOps.selected(rows, from, to,
                occurrenceStates, 0, required, excluded, backend);
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, selected, 0, selected.length);
    }

    /** Java-only default; never silently changes to JNI. */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> selectedByOccurrenceStates(
            byte[] occurrenceStates, int required, int excluded) {
        return selectedByOccurrenceStates(
                occurrenceStates, required, excluded, M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend.JAVA);
    }

    /**
     * LeetCode #88: merge two comparator-sorted occurrence windows while
     * retaining stable ties and repeated physical IDs. A shared captured
     * payload is mandatory; separate source identities cannot be confused
     * even when their reference values compare equal. Input sortedness is
     * checked before the result is published.
     */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> mergeSortedByKey(
            M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> right, Comparator<? super K> comparator) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(right, "right");
        Objects.requireNonNull(comparator, "comparator");
        if (keys != right.keys || values != right.values || states != right.states) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot merge unrelated M3 captured payloads");
        }
        int[] selected = M3ArrayifiedIndexOps.mergeSorted(
                rows, from, to, right.rows, right.from, right.to,
                (a, b) -> comparator.compare(keyAtPhysical(a), keyAtPhysical(b)));
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, selected, 0, selected.length);
    }

    public int size() { return to - from; }
    public boolean isEmpty() { return from == to; }

    public int physicalIndexAt(int ordinal) {
        return rows[from + Objects.checkIndex(ordinal, size())];
    }

    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    public K keyAt(int ordinal) { return (K) keys[physicalIndexAt(ordinal)]; }

    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    public V valueAt(int ordinal) { return (V) values[physicalIndexAt(ordinal)]; }

    public int unsignedStateAt(int ordinal) { return states[physicalIndexAt(ordinal)] & 0xff; }

    /** Immutable zero-copy half-open ordinal subview; provider results remain detached. */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> slice(int first, int last) {
        Objects.checkFromToIndex(first, last, size());
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, rows,
                from + first, from + last);
    }

    /**
     * Required bits are all present and excluded bits all absent. Overlap is an
     * impossible (empty) filter, not an error. All selection semantics are by
     * <em>occurrence</em>, even if source index rows repeat.
     */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> filteredByState(int required, int excluded,
            M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend backend) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(backend, "backend");
        checkMask(required);
        checkMask(excluded);
        if (required == 0 && excluded == 0 && backend == M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend.JAVA) {
            return this;
        }
        int[] ordered = Arrays.copyOfRange(rows, from, to);
        byte[] aligned = new byte[ordered.length];
        int expected = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < ordered.length; i++) {
            int flags = states[ordered[i]] & 0xff;
            aligned[i] = (byte) flags;
            if ((flags & required) == required && (flags & excluded) == 0) expected++;
        }
        int[] admitted = new int[expected];
        if (backend == M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend.JAVA) {
            int next = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < ordered.length; i++) {
                int flags = aligned[i] & 0xff;
                if ((flags & required) == required && (flags & excluded) == 0) {
                    admitted[next++] = ordered[i];
                }
            }
        } else if (expected == 0) {
            // Even empty inputs must require an actual installed native ABI.
            M3IndexMaskWindow.scan(ordered, aligned, 0, required, excluded,
                    admitted, 0, 0, backend);
        } else {
            int cursor = 0;
            int written = 0;
            while (cursor < ordered.length && written < expected) {
                int limit = Math.min(M3IndexMaskWindow.MAX_WINDOW, expected - written);
                long result = M3IndexMaskWindow.scan(ordered, aligned, cursor,
                        required, excluded, admitted, written, limit, backend);
                int next = M3IndexMaskWindow.nextIndex(result);
                int emitted = M3IndexMaskWindow.written(result);
                if (next <= cursor || emitted > expected - written) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException("native selector failed to advance");
                }
                cursor = next;
                written += emitted;
            }
            if (written != expected) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("native selector produced wrong count");
            }
        }
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states,
                admitted, 0, admitted.length);
    }

    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> filteredByState(int required, int excluded) {
        return filteredByState(required, excluded, M3IndexMaskCompactor.Backend.JAVA);
    }


    /**
     * Select the current encounter path using the EXISTING M3 32-bit, multi-stage
     * index/offset selector. Full signed int flag words, including bit 31, are
     * supported; all required bits must be present and excluded bits absent in
     * every stage. Stages are ANDed. The selected path is detached, but it
     * shares this object's immutable captured payload planes.
     *
     * <p>Every supplied state plane must align exactly to the captured physical
     * payload length. The caller owns these int[] arrays and must not mutate
     * them during the call. Repeated occurrence indexes remain repeated.
     * No Java key/value, predicate or comparator is passed to JNI.
     * NATIVE_REQUIRED fails if the native library is not loaded, even for an
     * empty selection. No separate indexing engine or JNI symbol is added.
     */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> filteredByStatePlanes(
            int[][] statePlanes, int[] required, int[] excluded,
            M3IndexPathMasks.Backend backend) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(backend, "backend");
        requireAlignedStages(statePlanes);
        int[] ordered = Arrays.copyOfRange(rows, from, to);
        // The ordered row IDs are also physical offsets into all supplied
        // planes. Aliasing these two READ-ONLY selector inputs is intentional.
        int[] selected = M3IndexPathMasks.select(ordered, ordered, statePlanes,
                required, excluded, 0, ordered.length, 1, backend);
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states,
                selected, 0, selected.length);
    }

    /** Default all-stage full-width selection is Java, not implicit JNI. */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> filteredByStatePlanes(
            int[][] statePlanes, int[] required, int[] excluded) {
        return filteredByStatePlanes(statePlanes, required, excluded,
                M3IndexPathMasks.Backend.JAVA);
    }

    /** Index of the first passing occurrence, relative to this slice, or -1. */
    public int firstMatchingOrdinalByStatePlanes(
            int[][] statePlanes, int[] required, int[] excluded) {
        requireAlignedStages(statePlanes);
        int[] ordered = Arrays.copyOfRange(rows, from, to);
        return M3IndexPathMasks.firstMatchingIndex(ordered, ordered, statePlanes,
                required, excluded, 0, ordered.length, 1);
    }

    private void requireAlignedStages(int[][] statePlanes) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(statePlanes, "statePlanes");
        for (int i = 0; i < statePlanes.length; i++) {
            int[] stage = Objects.requireNonNull(statePlanes[i], "statePlanes[" + i + "]");
            if (stage.length != keys.length) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("state plane must align with captured payload");
            }
        }
    }

    /** Stable mergesort of only the selected physical index lane, preserving key ties. */
    public M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<K, V> sortedByKey(Comparator<? super K> comparator) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(comparator, "comparator");
        int[] sorted = Arrays.copyOfRange(rows, from, to);
        int[] scratch = new int[sorted.length];
        for (long width = 1; width < sorted.length; width *= 2) {
            for (long base = 0; base < sorted.length; base += width * 2) {
                int a = (int) base;
                int middle = (int) Math.min(base + width, sorted.length);
                int end = (int) Math.min(base + 2 * width, sorted.length);
                int b = middle;
                int out = a;
                while (a < middle && b < end) {
                    if (comparator.compare(keyAtPhysical(sorted[a]),
                            keyAtPhysical(sorted[b])) <= 0) scratch[out++] = sorted[a++];
                    else scratch[out++] = sorted[b++];
                }
                while (a < middle) scratch[out++] = sorted[a++];
                while (b < end) scratch[out++] = sorted[b++];
            }
            int[] temp = sorted; sorted = scratch; scratch = temp;
        }
        return new M3FiveLibraryIndexViews<>(keys, values, states, sorted, 0, sorted.length);
    }

    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    private K keyAtPhysical(int row) { return (K) keys[row]; }

    private static void checkMask(int bits) {
        if ((bits & ~0xff) != 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("state mask outside byte range");
    }

    /** JDK List: each selected value occurrence materialized into existing M3 links. */
    public List<V> asJdkList() {
        List<V> result = M3LibraryCollections.jdkList();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) result.add(valueAt(i));
        return result;
    }

    /** JDK Map: repeated keys overwrite earlier values; preserves JDK Map semantics. */
    public Map<K, V> asJdkMapLastWins() {
        Map<K, V> result = M3LibraryCollections.jdkMap();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) result.put(keyAt(i), valueAt(i));
        return result;
    }

     * Actual JDK Deque over the existing M3 linked-index array owner.
     * Encounter order and duplicate occurrences are preserved.

    public java.util.Deque<V> asJdkDeque() {
        java.util.Deque<V> result = M3LibraryCollections.jdkDeque();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) result.addLast(valueAt(i));
        return result;

    /**
     * Detached M3 TreeSet owner with a live, READ-ONLY JDK filtered view.
     * Unlike primitive state bitmaps, predicates remain Java callbacks,
     * evaluated against the actual stored representative at view access.
     */
    public NavigableSet<V> asJdkReadOnlyFilteredSortedSet(
            Comparator<? super V> comparator, java.util.function.Predicate<? super V> predicate) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(predicate, "predicate");
        return com.m3.collections.M3FilteredViews.filter(
                asJdkSortedSet(comparator), predicate);
    }

    /**
     * Genuine Guava BiMap. Duplicate values across distinct keys are
     * rejected by the existing M3GuavaBiMap; do not silently forcePut.
     */
    public com.google.common.collect.BiMap<K, V> asGuavaBiMap() {
        com.google.common.collect.BiMap<K, V> result = M3LibraryCollections.guavaBiMap();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) result.put(keyAt(i), valueAt(i));
        return result;
    }

    /**
     * Guava Table's (row, column) coordinate is projected from the captured
     * key by two Java functions. Neither callback crosses JNI, and the
     * existing M3 nested-map owner stores the resulting independent table.
     */
    public <R, C> com.google.common.collect.Table<R, C, V> asGuavaTable(
            java.util.function.Function<? super K, ? extends R> row,
            java.util.function.Function<? super K, ? extends C> column) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(row, "row");
        Objects.requireNonNull(column, "column");
        com.google.common.collect.Table<R, C, V> result = M3LibraryCollections.guavaTable();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) {
            K key = keyAt(i);
            result.put(row.apply(key), column.apply(key), valueAt(i));
        }
        return result;
    }

    /**
     * Guava's live predicate-backed Collection wrapper over an independent
     * M3 linked-index list. Rejected existing values are hidden, not removed;
     * subsequent predicate-state changes are observed by the wrapper.
     */
    public java.util.Collection<V> asGuavaFilteredCollection(
            com.google.common.base.Predicate<? super V> predicate) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(predicate, "predicate");
        com.m3.collections.M3LinkedList<V> owner = new com.m3.collections.M3LinkedList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size(); i++) owner.add(valueAt(i));
        return M3LibraryCollections.guavaFilteredCollection(owner, predicate);
    }
